summary: Package ships Linux binary with WebRTC/WebSocket-relayed PTY backdoor
details: The npm package ships a Linux/amd64 Go binary (bin/sxt) that opens a WebRTC data channel via a hardcoded signaling relay at wss://relay.sextant.top and pipes remote bytes into an interactive /bin/sh or /bin/bash PTY (via creack/pty + os/exec), giving whoever controls the relay full-host remote shell access on the installer's machine. On startup the binary also queries ip-api.com/json/ for host geolocation, ISP, and organization fields and POSTs registration data to https://relay.sextant.top/install, fingerprinting each installer host for the relay operator. package.json declares its license as 'SEE LICENSE IN https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control' and the binary contains 'claude-control' / 'claude-controlworkspace' strings, matching a covert remote-agent pattern rather than a documented CLI tool. The relay endpoint is hardcoded and not caller-configurable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
